full_judgment:
Ms. Syeda Afsar Jahan, J:- This first miscellaneous appeal arises from the judgment and order No.70 dated 19.09.2000 passed by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge. Court, Mymensingh in Miscellaneous Case  No.106A of 1997, rejecting the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case. 

 2. The petitioner as a plaintiff filed T.S. No.37 of 1995, before the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, 1st  Court, Mymensingh against the defendant Nos.I-8, for declaration. The defendant Nos.7-9, appeared and filed written statement, in the suit, which was fixed for hearing on 11.8.1997. The plaintiff filed an application for adjournment on that date i.e. on 11.08.1997, but his lawyer was engaged in another court, he could not move the application. The learned Sub-Ordinate Judge rejected said application at 10.30 am, directed the plaintiff to be ready for hearing at once. The learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, 1° Court, Mymensingh, thereafter dismissed the suit for default at 1.30 p.m. Immediately thereafter, the plaintiff's learned Advocate filed another application praying for adjournment at 2.35 p.m. but it was not considered by the court below. The plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Case No.I06A of 1997 on 26.8.1997, under Order IX, Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the order of dismissal dated 11.8.1997. The defendants opposed the case for restoration by filing a written objection denying the statement made in the application for setting aside the dismissal order. 

 3. The plaintiff-appellant was examined, as PW.1 in support of his case who produced -medical certificate and on the side of opposite party, DW.I was examined. Thereafter, the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Mymensingh by the order dated 19.09.2000, rejected the Miscellaneous Case No.106A of 1997. 

 4. Mr. lmran Siddiq, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of Mr. Mohammod Hossain, the learned Advocate for the appellant submits that the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, lst  Court, Mymensingh misread and misconstrued the evidence adduced by the plaintiff-appellant in the case and thereby erred in law in disallowing the Miscellaneous Case. lie further submits that the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, 1st  Court, erred in law in disallowing the miscellaneous case upon taking into consideration of the merit of the suit, and the court erred in disallowing the Miscellaneous Case in spite of the facts that the plaintiff-appellant could not appear on 11.08.1997 when the suit was called on, due to his illness and rain fall, and the plaintiff-appellant had no negligence or malafide motive in conducting the suit and as such the learned court below should have allowed the miscellaneous case. The non appearance on the part of the plaintiff on 11.8.1997 was unintentional and in view of the unintentional failure of the plaintiff-appellant to appear in the suit the justice demands that the original suit should be restored to its original file and number, by setting aside the dismissal order dated 11.8.1997. The appellant proved that there was sufficient cause for his none appearance. In the present case the appellant filed the application under Order IX Rule 9, along with his medical certificate -to show that he was sick on 11.8.1997 for , which he could not appear when the suit was called for hearing. 

 5. The learned Advocate for the appellant submits that the plaintiff filed an application for adjournment on 11.8.1997, which was rejected at 10.30 a.m. and the plaintiff was directed to get ready immediately. Thereafter, the court dismissed the suit for default at 1.30 p.m., when the record shows that the appellant filed another application for adjournment with a copy to the respondents at 2.35 p.m., but the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, l" Court, Mymensingh had already dismissed the Other Suit No.37 of 1995. The learned Advocate submits that the courts working hour starts from 10.30 am ends at 4.30 pm and he submits that since the petitioner filed an application for adjournment and rejecting same the learned court directed the plaintiff to get ready the court ought to have waited till the end of the day for passing final order on that day. In support of his submission, he cited a decision reported in AIR, 1928 (Alahabad) 301, (the case of Ram Shankar Tewari -Versus- Ram Narayan Tewari). 

 6. The learned Advocate for the appellant further submits that this court may allow his appeal by awarding a cost under the amended, provision of CPC, tinder Act No.8 of 2006, and submits that the Act is retrospective in the sense and it applies to the proceedings at the time when the Act came into force. In support of his submission he submitted that the miscellaneous appeal arises out of a proceedings filed under Order IX Rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure and the amended provision of law is applicable in the present appeal having arises on the same proceedings which is the continuation of the suit. The statute is retrospective, it deals with matters of procedure, the parliament has shown intention that the Act should operate in pending proceedings and the court of appeal is entitled to give effect to this retrospective intent of the legal right in the present case and in support of his submissions he placed decision of case, reported in 17 DLR (SC) 23 (the case of Sayedur Rahman —Versus- The Chief Election Commissioner), 11 MLR (AD) 343 (the case of Md. Khaleque Islam —Versus-The State), AIR 1966 (SC) 1423 (the case of Dayawati and another —Versus- Indrojit and others) and 48 DLR (AD) 6 (the case of Abdul Wadud —Versus- The State). 

 7. Mr. Abu Bakar Siddique, the learned Advocate appearing for they respondents, submits that the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge rightly rejected the appellant's Miscellaneous Case No.106A of 1997 under Order IX, Rule 9 of CPC, on perusal of the evidence and there is no need to interfere with the order dated 19.9.2000 passed by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, Court, Mymensingh - in Miscellaneous Case No.I06A of 1997 and he further submits that the subsequent amendment of the Code of Civil. Procedure is not applicable in the present case. 

 8. Heard the learned Advocate and, perused the evidence on record. We have examined the records. We find that the plaintiff-appellant filed an application for adjournment of hearing on 11.8.1997, which was rejected at 10,30 a. m. and the learned court directed the parties to get ready for hearing at once and the case was subsequently dismissed for default at 01.30 p. m. The plaintiff took steps at 2.35 p. m. and filed an application for adjournment serving copy thereof to the other side, but it was not considered. The plaintiff on 26.8.1997, filed Miscellaneous Case for restoration of the suit after setting aside the dismissal order dated 11.8.1997. The plaintiff-appellant tried to prove his sickness by producing medical certificate for which sickness he was prevented from appearing on the date of hearing on 11.8.1997. The plaintiff proved his cause for none appearance on the date fixed, when the suit was called on for hearing. 

 9. We have gone through the amended provision of the Code of Civil Procedure (Act No.8 of 2006), inserting 9A directly setting aside dismissal. We have seen from the record that the Miscellaneous Case No.106A of 1997 was filed on 26.8,1997 for setting aside the dismissal order dated 11.8.1997, within a period of 30(thirty) days. Upon relying the decisions in the case of "Sayedur Rahman -Versus- The Chief Election Commissioner, Dhaka", reported in page-23, 17 DLR (SC), case of "Md. Khaleque Islam -Versus- The State" reported in page-343, 11 MLR (AD), the case of "Dayawati and another -Versus-Indrojit and others" reported in AIR 1906 page-I428 (Panjab), the case of "Abdul Wadud -Versus- The State" reported in page-6, 48 DLR (AD) and thecase of "Dulal Chandra and others -Vs- Banamali Guchant" reported in page-92, AIR 1989 Calcutta and the decision of the case "Attorney General -Vs- Vernazza" at page-101 All England Reports 1960 by the plaintiff-appellant. We find substance in the submission of the learned Advocate and in spit in the appeal. The amended provision 23BLT(HCD) 2015 Ashraf Uddin Ahmed V of the Act 8 of 2006 in respect of 9A of the Rule 9 of Order IX of the Code of Civil Procedure is applicable in the appeal and the appeal may be allowed on payment of cost. Thus we are inclined to allow the appeal. The judgment and order dated 19.9.2000 passed by the learned Sub-Ordinate Judge, 1st  Court, Mymensingh in Miscellaneous Case No.lO6A of 1997 is set aside subject to payment of Tk.1,000/- (one thousand) only to the respondent and the suit is restored to its original file and number.
